proposed.statement: For every \(0<h\leq1/4\), both members of \(P_h^{\mathrm{pair}}=(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{1,1,1,2,L}\), and \[|\theta(P_{1,h})-\theta(P_{0,h})|=h^2/8,\qquad \operatorname{TV}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})=h^4/96,\qquad \operatorname{KL}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\leq h^5/240.\] For \(n\geq4^5\), \(h=n^{-1/5}\) gives the clean two-point lower rate \(n^{-2/5}\), while \(h=1/4\) covers the remaining finite set of sample sizes after adjusting the constant. With \(h=\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}^{1/4}/4\), the explicit contaminants satisfy \(R_h=(1-\epsilon)P_{0,h}+\epsilon Q_{0,h}=(1-\epsilon)P_{1,h}+\epsilon Q_{1,h}\), and the clean targets are separated by a constant multiple of \(\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}^{1/2}\).

proposed.statement: On the full declared class with \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1\), and \(\kappa=2\), there exist \(c_0,C_0>0\), depending only on \(L\), such that jointly for every \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\), \[c_0\{n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\}\leq\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;1,1,1,2,L)\leq\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{1,1,1,2,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_{\mathrm{Lip}}-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\{n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\}.\] When \(b_n\leq1/4\), the sharper pre-optimization bound is \[\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{1,1,1,2,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_{\mathrm{Lip}}-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\left[h_n^2+(nh_n)^{-1/2}+\epsilon h_n^{-2}+\exp\{-c_0nh_n^{7/2}\}\right].\] For each body cell \(D\subseteq[r_j,2r_j]\), writing \(q_D=Q\{X\in D\}\), its weighted contamination shift is at most \(C_0\epsilon q_D/r_j^2\), and \(\sum_Dq_D\leq1\); the reused boundary slab \(B_n\) contributes at most \(C_0\epsilon q_{B_n}/h_n^2\). These bounds depend only on total contaminating mass and therefore cover both point masses and diffuse within-cell contamination. The estimator uses \(O(n\log(1/h_n)+h_n^{-1})\) arithmetic operations and \(O(h_n^{-1})\) memory.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For d greater than one, beta different from one, or alpha below one, construct a total finite data-only robust slabwise projected correction whose nuisance pilots and Gram matrices remain uniformly controlled above stable local occupancy, or prove a same-class interaction lower bound; then optimize every remaining balance, including equality-case logarithms.
open_obligations.obstruction: The all-kappa cell proof uses one-dimensional Lipschitz covariance bias and direct boundary reconstruction. Outside that subfamily, the frozen projection handle states no quantitative robustness inequality. A point or diffuse contaminant in one fine projected cell leaves an epsilon-squared kernel-diagonal term growing with projection dimension and inverse overlap; coordinatewise robustification does not control all pair terms below stable local occupancy, while occupancy truncation can erase the clean high-resolution gain. This is estimator-specific and therefore is not itself a minimax interaction converse.
open_obligations.attempted: The projected nuisance-product identity was expanded under point and diffuse within-cell contamination. Clean degeneracy removes first-order pilot bias, but the contaminated Hoeffding expectation retains the epsilon-squared diagonal. Range bounds force a projection resolution below that needed for the clean fast-functional correction, and anomaly filtering prevents this failure from serving as a universal lower-bound witness.

prose_updates.tldr: On the exact one-dimensional boundary class with Lipschitz outcome regressions and propensity calibration smoothness at least one, one total finite dyadic cell estimator attains the same-experiment minimax risk \(r_{n,\kappa}+\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\) for every \(\kappa>0\). The clean term is parametric below \(\kappa=1\), equals \(\{\log(en)/n\}^{1/2}\) at the elbow, and is \(n^{-2/(\kappa+3)}\) above it. The theorem proves that clean functional efficiency and the contamination modulus are simultaneously attainable on this subfamily; the higher-dimensional or non-Lipschitz smoothness interactions remain open.

project_justification.gap: The clean weak-overlap literature does not provide a same-experiment minimax theorem when an arbitrary Huber contaminant may replace \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). In particular, the Ma--Sant'Anna--Sasaki--Ura clean conditions and this exact known-design polynomial-boundary contamination experiment are incomparable, so their asymptotic results and converses do not transfer automatically. No located result gives the all-\(\kappa\) clean elbow together with the full-record contamination radius on this declared class.
project_justification.niche: The missing benchmark is a boundary reconstruction whose variance changes correctly across the integrable, logarithmic, and nonintegrable inverse-overlap regimes while remaining stable when all contaminating mass is placed in its lowest-occupancy slab.
project_justification.fill: The variable-width dyadic estimator has error envelope \(h^2+n^{-1/2}V_\kappa(h)^{1/2}+\epsilon h^{-\kappa}+\exp\{-cnh^{\kappa+3/2}\}\). Optimizing its explicit cutoff yields the complete one-dimensional phase diagram, and exact clean-law pairs plus Huber-neighborhood collisions give matching same-experiment lower bounds.

prose_updates.related_work: MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 is the nearest clean-record comparator: its Section 3 estimator and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 operate under clean i.i.d. sampling, whereas the present benchmark permits arbitrary joint replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). Its weak-overlap conditions and this exact uniform-design polynomial-boundary experiment are incomparable, so no published converse transfers automatically. KhanTamer2010 explains support-tail irregularity but not this controlled boundary class or its contamination phase. ChenGaoRen2016 supplies the Huber-neighborhood testing template, not the scalar ATE estimator that preserves the clean functional rate. RobinsEtAl2017HOEE, LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF, and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024 motivate the still-open higher-dimensional projected route under clean sampling. HaradaFujisawa2024 treats outcome outliers under stronger overlap, AgarwalSingh2022 assumes structured corruption with bounded propensity, and neither covers arbitrary full-record contamination at a propensity zero. SasakiUra2022ET and SasakiUra2022Robustate motivate trimming and boundary correction; the right-heart-catheterization analysis is a consumer of the theoretical benchmark, not evidence that its records are corrupted or that its parametric propensity belongs to this class.
prose_updates.interpretation: The overlap exponent controls the clean price through the summability of inverse treated-cell mass. When \(\kappa<1\), that sum is finite and root-\(n\) risk remains possible; at \(\kappa=1\), contributions from all dyadic scales accumulate a square-root logarithm; above one, the lowest retained slab dominates and produces \(n^{-2/(\kappa+3)}\). Corruption has a different balance: a boundary slab of width \(h\) amplifies adversarial mass by \(h^{-\kappa}\), so balancing it with Lipschitz boundary bias yields \(\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\). One bandwidth attains both terms, so there is no additional nuisance--contamination interaction penalty on this subfamily.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The direct cell argument relies on one-dimensional Lipschitz covariance bias and boundary reconstruction. For a boundary cell \(B=[h,2h]\), clean treated mass is of order \(h^{\kappa+1}\), so either point or diffuse contaminating mass \(q_B\) shifts its weighted contribution by at most order \(\epsilon q_Bh^{-\kappa}\); at \(h=\epsilon^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) this equals the squared boundary bias. In higher dimension or under other smoothness orders, preserving the clean projected functional gain requires robust high-resolution nuisance and Gram estimation that is not proved here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The headline is the exact one-dimensional result for \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), every \(\alpha\geq1\), and every \(\kappa>0\): \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon)\asymp r_{n,\kappa}+\epsilon^{2/(\kappa+2)}\), with a total finite estimator, the \(\kappa=1\) logarithm, and matching same-experiment converses. The former quadratic theorem is retained as a corollary. The cases \(d>1\), \(\beta\neq1\), or \(\alpha<1\), their interactions, and their remaining equality-case logarithms are open. Fixed nonzero contamination leaves irreducible ambiguity; no claim identifies \(\theta(P)\) from \(R\), and no claim says the Sasaki--Ura application is contaminated or satisfies this exact benchmark class.
